items.title: How customers reach Moksy support
items.body: Moksy's contact-support page says most answers are in the help centre, and when they are not, this is how you reach a person. Support is support@moksy.ai. The page says to include the account email and, if it is about a specific plan or review, the link to it, which roughly halves the number of messages it takes to fix something. The fastest route by problem: account or sign-in goes to support (if the customer cannot sign in at all, they say so from the address on the account); a plan that looks wrong goes to support, saying which section and mentioning if a reviewer has been involved; billing or credit goes to support with the date and amount of the charge; a review or a dispute goes to support, and disputed reviews are arbitrated by a senior reviewer; privacy or data requests go to privacy@moksy.ai, which reaches the people who handle them directly; something broken goes to support with what the customer did and what happened (a screenshot is worth several paragraphs). Someone buying rather than fixing is sent to Sales, which handles pricing, procurement and security questionnaires. Legal questions about the terms go to legal@moksy.ai. Source: contact-support.json, legal-terms.json.

items.title: Plans, limits and what each includes
items.body: Moksy's published plans (GBP per month): Free £0 gives 3 projects, a Starter Blueprint of 5 of 22 areas, standard Moksy models, reading published reviewer work and 1 seat, with 5 exports a month, no Expert Reviews and no API access. Pro £19 gives 25 projects, a Fuller Blueprint of 12 of 22 areas, advanced models, unlimited Expert Reviews, 5 seats, 100 exports a month and API access. Max £79 gives unlimited projects, a Complete Blueprint of all 22 areas, the most capable models, unlimited Expert Reviews, unlimited seats and unlimited exports, with API access, and Max is the plan that makes someone eligible to become a paid reviewer. The pricing page says the Free plan is a real plan, the same engine reporting on fewer areas (five of the twenty-two, chosen for what you are building), deliberately enough to judge whether the thinking is any good. Pro is the first tier an accredited reviewer can read your plan on. Enterprise and public sector are priced separately and include SSO and SCIM, role-based access, a signed DPA, invoicing against a PO, UK data residency and a private reviewer pool; public bodies get procurement paperwork and discounted credit. Moksy claims no rights over a customer's plan or the idea behind it, on any tier. Source: pricing.json, pages/pricing-mox.json.

items.title: MOX credit, refunds and the wallet
items.body: MOX is Moksy credit; per the lexicon 1 MOX equals $0.01. The pricing pages say a membership is a monthly plan that carries what is included in it and renews on its own, while MOX is credit bought once and spent when the customer chooses, for work outside those benefits: expert reviews, additional plans and priority turnaround. Nobody needs to buy MOX to produce a plan. MOX does not renew on its own, is dollar-pegged so the price of a review does not move with the customer's currency, and every debit is itemised in the wallet ledger so a customer can see what a piece of work cost after it happened. On team tiers MOX is pooled: one balance for the workspace rather than a card per person. There are no expiry surprises: balance and history stay visible in the wallet. On refunds, the page says only: can I get a refund on unused credit? Contact support and we will look at it. That is a discretionary review, not a promise of an automatic refund. Source: pages/pricing-mox.json, pricing.json, Moksy Lexicon.

questions.prompt: A customer writes: "The cost figures in my Moksy plan were wrong. I used them to book a supplier and it cost me. I want a refund." Write the reply you would send and say what you would do internally, using only what Moksy has published.
questions.answer: I'm sorry this has caused you a problem, and thank you for telling us. I want to be clear about how Moksy describes its plans: a plan is an AI-drafted draft, every recommendation shows its reasoning, and the Terms say AI output is for information only and must be reviewed and validated before relying on it; an accredited reviewer can correct a plan, and Expert Reviews are included from Pro upward. I cannot promise a refund in this message. I am passing your case to the right people with your account email and the link to the plan, and we will come back to you. If any MOX credit is unused you can also ask us to look at that. Internally I would record the plan link, the section with the wrong figures and what was booked, escalate rather than decide a refund or liability myself (the Terms cap liability at what the customer paid in the previous 12 months, which is for the right people to apply), and flag if the figure should have been caught by review.
questions.rubric: A good answer: is empathetic; accurately restates that a plan is a draft, AI output is informational and must be validated, reviews exist and are included from Pro up; does not promise a refund or accept liability; does not invent a refund policy for subscription charges; mentions unused MOX credit can be looked at only if relevant; takes the details (account email, plan link, section, what was booked) and escalates; may mention the liability cap as something others apply. Penalise promising refunds or compensation, blaming the customer, or inventing policies.

items.title: Reviews, drafts and what the plan is
items.body: Moksy uses large language models to draft plans from the answers a customer gives. The trust page says two things plainly: an AI-drafted plan is a draft, and it is fluent, which is exactly what makes an unchecked one risky, which is why expert review exists. The pricing page says some of a plan will be wrong; every recommendation shows its reasoning instead of asserting an answer; and an accredited reviewer can correct it. Review requests are included from Pro upward. The Terms of Service say AI outputs are provided for informational purposes only, that Moksy does not guarantee their accuracy, completeness or fitness for purpose, and that the customer is solely responsible for reviewing and validating any AI-generated output before relying on it. Disputed reviews are arbitrated by a senior reviewer, and support is the route in. The help page's advice after a plan is generated: review the recommendations internally, refine the output if needed, then use the package to brief a supplier, compare options, or align your own delivery team, and use it as a working brief before committing budget. Source: pages/trust.json, pricing.json, legal-terms.json, help.json, contact-support.json.

items.title: Sign-in, sessions and what the messages mean
items.body: Moksy's error dictionary holds the messages customers actually see, and support should be able to say what each means. Examples: "Identity Verification Failed: Invalid email or password." (wrong sign-in details); "Your secure session has expired. Re-authentication is required." (sign in again); "Identity Suspended: Too many failed attempts. Contact administration." (the account is locked; the contact page's route is support, from the address on the account); "Multi-Factor Authentication required to proceed." (an extra verification step is needed); "That email already has a Moksy account. Try logging in instead." (the email is already registered); "Access Restricted: This feature is not included in your current subscription." (a plan limit, not a fault); "Authority Denied: You do not have the required role for this module." (a role or permission, not a plan); "Restricted Access: You have read-only permissions for this resource." (a read-only role); "The request exceeded the 10,000ms safety threshold" (a timeout); "The platform is currently undergoing scheduled governance. Check back shortly." (maintenance mode); "A critical system update is available. Please refresh your interface." (refresh the page); and "An unexpected orchestration error occurred. Our engineers have been alerted." (an internal error: ask what the customer did and what happened). Administrators must use two-factor authentication. Source: errors.json, contact-support.json, trust.json.

questions.prompt: A customer writes from a personal address: "I keep getting 'Identity Suspended: Too many failed attempts. Contact administration.' Please unlock my account." The account was registered under a different email address. Write your reply.
questions.answer: Thanks for getting in touch, and sorry for the trouble. That message means the account has been locked after too many failed sign-in attempts. To help with account and sign-in problems we ask customers to write to us from the address on the account, so please send your message to support@moksy.ai from the email address you registered with and tell us you cannot sign in. If you are not sure which address you used, tell us what you remember about when you created it and we will take it from there. Please do not send us your password.
questions.rubric: A good answer: explains the message means a lock after too many failed attempts; asks them to write to support from the address on the account (the published route); does not unlock or confirm account details for an unverified address; offers a helpful next step if they are unsure which email they used; asks them never to send a password; is polite and plain. Penalise unlocking the account on request, promising outcomes, or asking for sensitive data such as passwords or card numbers.

items.title: Data, privacy and trust: what you may and may not say
items.body: Moksy's trust page states the answers to security questionnaires in writing. Primary data is held in the UK, and sub-processors are pinned to UK or EEA regions wherever the service supports it. Data is protected with TLS 1.2 or better in transit and AES-256 at rest for the primary database and its backups. Access is role-based with a per-endpoint audit log, quarterly access reviews and mandatory two-factor authentication for administrators. Moksy does not sell personal data and does not enrich it with third-party demographic feeds. Controllers are notified within 72 hours of Moksy becoming aware of a personal-data breach, as UK GDPR Article 33 requires. Audit and ledger rows are anonymised rather than deleted, for fraud detection and financial record-keeping. Moksy uses large language models to draft plans, covered by the Data Processing Agreement; adding a sub-processor takes 30 days' notice. The page says plainly what Moksy does not claim: it is not ISO 27001 certified, and it is not Cyber Essentials certified yet; when that changes the page will say so. The privacy policy says the data controller is Moksy AI Ltd (privacy@moksy.ai); it lists sub-processors OpenAI, Stripe, MongoDB Atlas and Redis; payment data is processed by Stripe (card numbers are not stored by Moksy); legal bases are contract, legitimate interests, consent for marketing and legal obligation; customers can ask for access, correction, deletion, to object or restrict, portability, and can complain to the ICO; only strictly necessary cookies are used without consent, and optional analytics cookies need explicit consent. Source: pages/trust.json, legal-privacy.json.

items.title: The Terms of Service in brief
items.body: Moksy's Terms of Service are an agreement with Moksy AI Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales. Accepting means agreeing to the terms and the privacy policy. Customers must create an account, are responsible for keeping their login credentials confidential and for all activity under the account, and must be at least 18; someone creating an account for an organisation represents that they have authority to bind it. Acceptable use forbids unlawful use, unauthorised access, reverse engineering, harmful or defamatory content and reselling or sublicensing access without written permission. Premium features need a paid subscription, billed in advance monthly or annually; prices are in GBP and exclude VAT unless stated; payments are processed by Stripe and authorise recurring charges until the customer cancels; a subscription can be cancelled any time in account settings. The customer keeps ownership of the data and content they submit, and gives Moksy a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to process it solely to provide the services. AI output is informational only and not guaranteed. Moksy's total liability for a claim is capped at the amount the customer paid in the 12 months before it, and it is not liable for indirect or consequential loss. English law and courts apply. Material changes are notified by email or a prominent notice, and continued use means acceptance. Questions go to legal@moksy.ai. Source: legal-terms.json.

items.title: Where the published pages disagree: confirm before quoting
items.body: Support should quote published pages, and the pages are the company's statements. As read on 11 October 2026, a few of them disagree or look out of date, and a support person should know where, so that they do not repeat a figure as settled. (1) Data deletion: the trust page says customer data is hard-deleted within 30 days of termination, while the privacy policy says personal data is deleted or anonymised within 90 days of account closure, except where retention is required by law (financial records: 7 years). Do not quote either as definitive; say you will confirm and route to privacy@moksy.ai. (2) Security questionnaires: the contact-support page says Sales handles them, while the trust page says to send the questionnaire to privacy@moksy.ai. Confirm the current route before promising one, and never answer security claims you cannot evidence. (3) Sector wording: the Terms and privacy policy describe Moksy as for the education sector, while the help, pricing and trust pages describe founders, teams, agencies, enterprises and the public sector; do not tell a founder Moksy is only for schools, and flag the outdated legal wording. (4) Review arbitration: the contact page says disputed reviews are arbitrated by a senior reviewer; the internal lexicon names a rung for it, so say "a senior reviewer" as published without naming a rung.
